source: Toprank Review Academy (TRA) Nursing Module – Complete Handout

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: How does hypomania differ from mania?
questions.rationale: Hypomania (about 4 days) is less severe; it does not impair functioning and has no psychotic features.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Hypomania (PDF p. 270)
questions.quote: Hypomanic episodes do not impairthe person's ability to function

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Major depressive episodes plus one or more hypomanic episodes, with no history of mania, indicate:
questions.rationale: Bipolar II: depression plus hypomania, never full mania; Bipolar I includes mania.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Bipolar Disorders (PDF p. 270)
questions.quote: One or more major depressive episode accompanied by at least one hypomanic episode

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Chronic, milder depressed mood lasting 2 years or more is:
questions.rationale: Dysthymia: at least 2 years of depressed mood less severe than major depression.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Dysthymic Disorder (PDF p. 270)
questions.quote: Characterized by at least 2 years of depressed mood

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Fall-onset seasonal affective disorder typically presents with:
questions.rationale: Winter SAD: hypersomnia, carbohydrate craving, weight gain; spring-onset has insomnia and weight loss.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Seasonal Affective Disorder (PDF p. 270)
questions.quote: People experience increased sleep

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: A mother on day 4 postpartum is tearful and anxious but caring for her baby. This most likely is:
questions.rationale: Postpartum blues are common, peak at 3–7 days, and resolve without medical treatment.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Postpartum Blues (PDF p. 271)
questions.quote: Peak in 3 to 7 days

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client starting lithium asks when it will work. The nurse says it usually takes about:
questions.rationale: Lithium's therapeutic effect becomes evident after about 10–14 days.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Lithium Therapy (PDF p. 271)
questions.quote: Take 10 -14 days before therapeutic effect becomes evident

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Which teaching helps prevent lithium toxicity?
questions.rationale: Adequate fluids and normal sodium intake; dehydration, sweating, or vomiting raise lithium levels.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Lithium Therapy (PDF p. 271)
questions.quote: Adequate amount of fluid (2-3 L/day)

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client on lithium has severe vomiting, diarrhea, and coarse tremors. The nurse should first:
questions.rationale: These are toxicity signs; hold lithium and report for serum level.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Lithium Therapy (PDF p. 271)
questions.quote: Severe nausea, vomiting diarrhea, muscle weakness & tremors

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A manic client cannot sit long enough to eat. The nurse should provide:
questions.rationale: Provide frequent high-calorie, high-protein finger foods the client can eat while moving.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Mania Interventions (PDF p. 271)
questions.quote: Frequently provide finger foods that are high in calories and protein

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Which measure promotes sleep in a manic client?
questions.rationale: Reduce stimulation and establish a bedtime routine.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Mania Interventions (PDF p. 271)
questions.quote: Promoterestandsleepby decreasing environmental stimulation

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Sudden blindness after a stressful event, with the client showing little concern, suggests:
questions.rationale: Conversion disorder shows sudden sensory or motor loss with 'la belle indifference.'
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Conversion Disorder (PDF p. 272)
questions.quote: La belle in difference, a seeming lack of concernor distress, is a key feature.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Preoccupation with an imagined defect, such as crooked teeth, is:
questions.rationale: Body dysmorphic disorder: preoccupation with an imagined or exaggerated physical defect.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Body Dysmorphic Disorder (PDF p. 272)
questions.quote: It is preoccupation with an imagined or exaggerated defect in physical appearance

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A prisoner fakes back pain to avoid a court hearing. This is:
questions.rationale: Malingering is intentional symptom production for external incentives like avoiding prosecution.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Malingering (PDF p. 272)
questions.quote: evading criminal prosecution

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A mother repeatedly makes her child ill to gain medical attention. This is:
questions.rationale: Munchausen by proxy: inflicting illness on another to gain attention; also child abuse.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Factitious Disorder (PDF p. 273)
questions.quote: Occurs when a person inflicts illness or injury on someone else

questions.subject: NP V
questions.topic: Concepts of Mental Health & Therapeutic Models
questions.stem: A client's family gives extra attention whenever he complains of pain. This illustrates:
questions.rationale: Secondary gain is an external benefit (attention); primary gain is relief of anxiety.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Psychosocial Theories (PDF p. 273)
questions.quote: attention from family members

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Which approach is best for a client with somatization disorder?
questions.rationale: Show empathy, keep one provider to avoid doctor shopping, and avoid early confrontation and narcotics.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Somatoform Management (PDF p. 273)
questions.quote: The health care provider must show empathy and sensitivity to the clients physical complaints

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Which is an emotion-focused coping strategy?
questions.rationale: Emotion-focused: relaxation, deep breathing, guided imagery, distraction; the rest are problem-focused.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Coping Strategies (PDF p. 274)
questions.quote: Guided imagery

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client needs more alcohol to get the same effect. This is:
questions.rationale: Tolerance means needing more of a substance for the same effect.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Substance Abuse Terms (PDF p. 274)
questions.quote: the patient needs more of the substance (alcohol) to produce same effect.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client functions while drinking but later has no memory of it. This is a:
questions.rationale: A blackout is functioning without conscious awareness or memory of behavior.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Substance Abuse Terms (PDF p. 274)
questions.quote: person continues to function but has no consciousawarenessof his or her behavior

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Alcohol withdrawal symptoms usually begin how long after the last drink?
questions.rationale: Withdrawal begins 4–12 hours after stopping and may last 1–2 weeks.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Alcohol Withdrawal (PDF p. 275)
questions.quote: to 12 hours after cessation or marked reduction of alcohol intake

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Which drug class manages alcohol withdrawal?
questions.rationale: Benzodiazepines (lorazepam, chlordiazepoxide, diazepam) prevent seizures and DTs.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Alcohol Withdrawal (PDF p. 275)
questions.quote: Administration of benzodiazepines

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client on disulfiram drinks beer. Which reaction should the nurse expect?
questions.rationale: Alcohol with disulfiram causes flushing, throbbing headache, sweating, vomiting, and severe hypotension.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Nursing Alert: Alcohol (PDF p. 280)
questions.quote: Throbbing headache

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Chronic alcohol use with thiamine deficiency can cause:
questions.rationale: Long-term alcohol use causes Wernicke's encephalopathy, Korsakoff's psychosis, cirrhosis, and pancreatitis.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Long-Term Alcohol Effects (PDF p. 275)
questions.quote: Wernicke's encephalopathy

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Which sedative overdose is more likely to be fatal?
questions.rationale: Barbiturate overdose can cause coma, respiratory arrest, and death; benzodiazepine overdose alone is rarely fatal.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Sedatives (PDF p. 276)
questions.quote: Can be lethal
